correction.text: all of present-day Odisha plus the Andhra coast, from 322 BCE: 'Core territory is all of present-day Odisha and part of northern Andhra Pradesh'

keyframe_review.note: 129,000 km2 for -318..-292 (the page gives no area). The shape holds 313 of Odisha's 568 cells plus 138 cells of the Andhra coast; the page says Kalinga's 'core territory is all of present-day Odisha and part of northern Andhra Pradesh', reaching 'at its widest' Chhattisgarh and the Amarkantak hills, and notes that sources put the northern limit at the Mahanadi, the Baitarani or the Ganges. The correction adds the 255 missing Odisha cells; the northern limit stays disputed. The state begins in -322, four years before the shape ('Kalingas broke away from the empire of Magadha in 322 BCE').

keyframe_review.note: 129,000 km2 for -291..-257, the same outline as -318 to within two cells. Years: the shape ends -262, because Ashoka annexed Kalinga in c. 261 BCE (Kalinga War page: 'Kalinga annexed by Mauryan Empire'); Cliopatria keeps the Kalinga row for five more years and adds its cells to the Maurya shape only in -256. Odisha added as for -318.

correction.text: Kalinga from 224 BCE: modern Odisha ('Kalinga (modern Odisha)', Maurya page) and the coast south of it as Cliopatria draws it

keyframe_review.note: 81,000 km2 for -225..-189: Cliopatria's re-emerged Kalinga is smaller than before (it drops 175 cells of the southern coast) and the page does not say why; it says only that Kalinga 'broke away from the Mauryan empire during the rule of Dasharatha in 224 BCE', so the shape starts -224. The Maurya shape of the time still holds 376 cells of northern Odisha; the correction returns all Odisha to Kalinga and leaves the southern coast as in Cliopatria (unverified). (fx-28: 'from' -224 set so the keyframe starts with the -224 gain; in -225 the Maurya ledger still holds Kalinga, 'broke away from the Mauryan empire during the rule of Dasharatha in 224 BCE'.)

The Mahameghavahana page, which does not date Kalinga's independence ('arose in Kalinga after the decline of the Maurya Empire'), gives the founder Mahameghavahana's regnal date as 170 BCE and Kharavela as 50 BCE in its infobox while calling Kharavela's inscription '2nd century BCE' and 'c. 1st-century BCE' elsewhere; no territorial change is dated in -188..-171. notes:
Group sa-02-a. Page budget: four pages (Kalinga region, Kalinga War, Mahameghavahana dynasty, Maurya Empire).

START AND END. Cliopatria starts in -318 and ends in -171. The page dates the break from Magadha to 322 BCE, so the state starts there. The end is Cliopatria's boundary with the Mahameghavahana row (-170); the Mahameghavahana page does not date Kalinga's independence or the dynasty's start except through the infobox regnal list (founder 170 BCE). Whether Kalinga and the Mahameghavahana are one state with a dynasty change (Kharavela calls himself 'supreme Lord of Kalinga') is for the colour agent; the successor link is recorded and the dissolve event is the only break.

GAP -260..-225. The state has no territory (annexed by the Mauryas); Cliopatria's Kalinga row also stops being a state in effect then, but keeps the shape to -257. Dossier events: loss -261, gain -224.

ODISHA. Cliopatria's shapes cover only 55 percent of Odisha; the page says the core is all of Odisha, so every shape is adjusted by a union with the Odisha province. The northern limit is disputed in the sources; the correction takes the province, no more. The southern coast is left as Cliopatria draws it (the second shape is smaller; the page gives no reason).

CAPITALS. Dantapura is the page's 'ancient capital' but undated and unlocated; its point is a placeholder (centroid of the Kalinga shape). Tosali's dates are an assumption from the Mahameghavahana infobox.

OPEN. Kharavela's dating and the Hathigumpha inscription (2nd or 1st century BCE) belong to the mahameghavahana-dynasty dossier. The Satavahana conquest of Kalinga in the 1st century BCE (Mahameghavahana page) is after this state ends.

GAZETTEER. All names exist (Odisha as admin1; Cliopatria shapes).
